title: Queens by Martyna Majok at MTC #queensplay #martynamajok #manhattanth...
transcript: Pulitzer winner Martyna Majok is back with another great play about people whose lives are often invisible but just as richly complex as anyone else's. This one is about a group of immigrant women living in a basement apartment in Queens. Seamlessly jumping between 2001, 2011, and 2017, we get a broad understanding of their individual immigration stories, their backgrounds, and their hopes for the future. It's a difficult topic to address because it's so vast, but this play has a remarkably strong focus and foundation. Every character is given just enough attention to provide their piece of the puzzle without opening any unnecessary side plots. I think this is possible because of how organically the interactions unfold between characters — it's a masterclass in show, not tell, providing a genuinely captivating plot. Structurally, it's also very satisfying, smartly holding some cards in Act 1, then going deeper in Act 2 with a flourish of reveals that pack a punch both dramatically and thematically. Martyna Majok has such a gift for writing dialogue that's devastating and hopeful, and this play beautifully captures how desperately we hold onto dreams, and sometimes our possessions by proxy. It's heavy, but the sprinkles of humor and consistently crisp direction keep it from crumbling under its own weight, as do the strong performances. Julia Lester and Marin Ireland are especially fantastic. Rounded out by some thoughtful and impactful design elements, this is a great production. Queens is currently running through the end of November at City Center. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
